jute plants are harvested when they are 4-6 months old, usually before the seedpods fully mature
sickle is commonly used to cut the jute stalks
plants are cut close to the ground or pulled out by hand
jute stalks are bundled together and prepared for the retting process, which separates the fibers from the woody stem

retting is the process of separating the jute fibers from the woody core of the plant. The harvested jute stalks are submerged in water (rivers, ponds, or canals) for 10 to 30 days, depending on water temperature and conditions
soft water is ideal for retting, and the quality of water impacts the fiber quality
after retting, the jute fibers become loosened and can be easily extracted
workers strip the outer layer of the jute stalk by hand, peeling the fibers away from the woody stem
use water to wash off any remaining plant material to get clean fibers
wash stripped fibres thoroughly in clean water to remove dirt, impurities, and any residual bark or stem
excess water is squeezed out from the fibers by hand or using simple tools
check fibres for uniformity and cleanliness during this process
spread out washed fibres and hung in the sun to dry for a few days
fibers are sorted according to length, color, and strength
fibers are grade into different quality levels, with finer, longer fibers being more valuable
bundle jute fibers into bales for storage or transport to jute mills
align the fibers and then spun into yarns and threads
weave jute yarn into fabric, which can be used for sacks, bags or textile
twist jute yarn into thicker strands like ropes or twines
